question: The Portuguese company Altri SGPS S.A., whose main business is the production of wood pulp and eucalyptus-based forestry products, has officially announced its intention to set up a soluble cellulose and vegetable fibre production plant in A Ulloa (Lugo), Spain.

The company hopes to obtain public funding of EUR 250 million through a strategic project for economic recovery and transformation (PERTE) industrial decarbonisation programme (NextGenerationEU). The project aims to install a water catchment system with a flow of 46 000 cubic metres per day.

In addition, the factory would discharge organic compounds (increasing total phosphorus and total nitrogen, as well as sulphates, all at high temperatures) into the river Ulla, which would affect a body of water 1.5 km away that already suffers from serious eutrophication problems.

The deterioration in the ecological status of the bodies of water concerned would jeopardise the environmental objectives relating to surface waters set out in Article 4(1), point (a), of the Water Framework Directive 2000/60/EC1. 1.

As this project represents a breach of the ‘do no significant harm’ (DNSH) principle and does not comply with several environmental objectives under Regulation (EU) 852/20202, such as the protection of water resources, does the Commission consider this project eligible for funding?
Also, does the Commission consider that this project is in line with Directive 2000/60/EC?

Directive 2000/60/EC of 23⁰October⁰2000 establishing a framework for Community action in the field of water policy, OJ L 327, 22.12.2000, p. 1. Regulation (EU) 2020/852 of 18 June 2020 on the establishment of a framework to facilitate sustainable investment, OJ L 198, 22.6.2020, p. 13.
answer: 1. Regarding the ‘do no significant harm’ (DNSH) principle, the measures related to PERTES (strategic project for economic recovery and transformation) in the Recovery and Resilience Plan of Spain (3) require that selection criteria ensure compliance with the DNSH principle and EU environmental regulation.

The fulfilment of the targets related to the PERTES, including the DNSH requirements, will be formally assessed by the Commission under the relevant upcoming payment requests. 2. The Water Framework Directive (WFD) (4) requires Member States to ensure good status of all water bodies.

Any project having an impact on the water bodies must undergo a full assessment under Article 4(7) WFD and be subject to an environmental impact assessment procedure in line with the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive (5), ensuring the permits include all the necessary conditions for compliance with the EU law.
The Spanish authorities are responsible for ensuring conditions to avoid the deterioration of the status of the affected water body and must take action if any deviation from the permits takes place.

The Commission is aware of the fact that the Galician competent authorities have recently opened a public consultation on the environmental impact assessment of the project and the concession for water abstraction from the Portodemouros reservoir (6). Based on the reporting by Spanish authorities on the second River Basin Management Plan (RBMP ) (7).

the heavily modified water body of Portodemouros reservoir (8) is in less than good ecological potential and it was subject to time extension up to 2021 to achieve the objectives under Article 4.4 due to technical feasibility. The Commission is currently assessing the third RBMP for the 2021-2027 cycle.
